text:
maya: quick brain dump / checkcall. i'm proposing a lightweight 'proxy-token' layer to reduce blast radius of project-scoped API keys. goal: incremental, low-friction migration that doesn't force a big rbac refactor up-front.

alex: sounds promising. what's the concrete shape and how does runtime validate without an extra sync call?

maya: core idea: auth-service mints signed short-lived proxy tokens after validating the original key. token contains compact scope (route groups), actor id, original_project (for billing), and a signature. runtime validates signature + nonce locally. no auth-service hop per request. TTLs vary by class.

sam: give an example token payload and a curl flow pls.

maya: example (base64 payload inside token):
```
{\n  "aid":"svc-payment",\n  "rg":["embed.read","models.infer"],\n  "exp":1744204834,\n  "proj":"proj-9a3f",\n  "kid":"sig-v2"\n}
```
mint flow (gateway):
```
POST /internal/mint-proxy
Auth: ApiKey <old-key>
Body: {actor:"svc-payment", desired_rg:["embed.read"]}
-> returns X-Proxy-Token: ptk_eyJ...
```
runtime validates signature using cached pubkey and checks rg mapping.

irene: important: don't put full original key id in token to avoid leakage. include a hashed key fingerprint for audit only (hash(salt + key_id)).

alex: performance wise, runtime will need fast signature checks. are we OK with RSA or prefer ed25519? also key rotation semantics?

maya: opt ed25519 for smaller sigs and faster verification. auth-service signs, stores private in KMS/HSM; runtime caches public keys and rotates on schedule. rotation is key-versioned (kid). tokens reference kid so runtime picks correct pubkey.

sam: migration strategy? we need a path that keeps customers running and gives us telemetry.

maya: propose phased rollout:
1) discovery mode (2w): gateway emits X-Proxy-Token for requests using legacy key but runtime still accepts legacy key. we log metrics: percent of calls with proxy vs legacy, top wildcard routes.
2) warn mode (2w): runtime starts emitting structured warnings in logs and admin console when legacy key used against broad routes.
3) enforce mode: runtime rejects legacy keys on broad-scope calls unless accompanied by proxy token. emergency admin bypass toggle for on-call.
4) long-term: deprecate legacy acceptance after N months.

irene: we should auto-generate route-groups and suggest minimal scopes for services based on historical access patterns to make migration easier. chaos: how to represent patterns without blowing token size?

maya: use short route-group ids (e.g., eg1, mi2) and a server-side registry mapping ids -> routes. token only carries group ids. group registry is small and cached by runtime.

sam: long-running background jobs? they can't refresh every 5 minutes.

maya: plan: two token classes: interactive (ttl 5m) and machine (ttl up to 12h) with stricter enrollment: machine tokens require enrollment record with owner, rotation schedule, and approval. also emit audits for each mint.

alex: good. security questions: what happens on auth-service compromise? how do we revoke quickly?

maya: revocation options:
- maintain a compact revocation bloom filter with recent revoked token nonces; runtime fetches periodically (seconds granularity).
- shorten machine-class TTLs for sensitive actors.
- emergency key rotation: rotate signing key and mark old tokens invalid. runtime will reject tokens with unknown kid.

irene: ops instrumentation: need metrics and dashboards: tokens_minted{service,env}, token_mint_lat, tokens_rejected_route{service,route_group}, legacy_key_usage_pct, migration_heatmap by service. also audit log with hashed key_fingerprint and mint_reason.

ops-bot: note: created dashboard template infra/proxy-token-migration. will add charts: token vs legacy over time, top rejected routes.

sam: rollout automation: provide a CLI to mint scoped tokens for testing and a console button to create scoped service tokens. also provide sample client libs to auto-refresh tokens.

maya: sample client refresh snippet:
```
while true:
  token = fetch_x_proxy_token()
  use token for requests
  sleep(token.exp - now - 10s)
```

alex: operationally we need per-project quotas and billing mapping preserved. original_project in token is fine for billing, but make sure runtime doesn't leak project id to downstream services unless needed. only include proj in metrics/audit.

irene: also add migration-mode header so we can A/B observability: X-Migration-Mode: discovery|warn|enforce.

maya: open questions for RFC:
- canonical format for route groups and normalization rules
- token compact encoding (base64 of JSON vs binary CBOR)
- TTL tiers and enrollment criteria for machine tokens
- revocation window and bloom filter size/refresh cadence
- admin bypass UX and audit trail

sam: I'll own the rollout checklist + audit requirements. alex, can you review crypto choices and key lifecycle?

alex: yes. i'll vet ed25519 vs other, KMS integration, and rotation cadence.

maya: i'll draft an RFC covering data model, mint flow, token format, migration phases, and dashboards. will aim to post by Thursday EOD.

deploy-bot: staging canary: svc-payments called /v1/embeddings with proxy token at 2024-09-13T10:10Z :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: smoke test run scheduled for 2024-09-14 02:00Z in staging (will simulate long-running clients).

alex: thanks everyone. let's try to keep the initial rollout permissive enough to avoid customer outages but strict enough to get meaningful telemetry.

maya: agreed. one final note: this approach is intentionally a runtime shim so we can later converge on a single RBAC grammar once teams are ready. for now minimal invasiveness. :+1:
